learning.title: A green Bakery CI can be a metadata run that executed no code lane
learning.trigger: A PR's Bakery CI concludes success while fast / format, fast / typecheck and fast / focused unit all read SKIPPED; the aggregate reports success over lanes that never ran.
learning.rule: Two mechanisms combine. (1) scripts/ci/classify-changes.ts routeForEventAction returns 'metadata' for a pull_request event whose action is 'edited' - deliberately, so a body-only fix never pays for a full run; the workflow's 'edited' trigger and its separate concurrency group exist for that case. (2) A push whose gate jobs are still running is CANCELLED by a later run on the same ref (the shared concurrency group), and it is the push run that would have run the code lanes. So: push, then edit the body while the gate is running, and the gate run dies while an 'edited' run takes over, succeeds, and shows green. The aggregate check then reports success over zero executed code lanes, because a skipped lane is not a failure. This bit the same seat twice in one night on two different PRs. The cure: a green is evidence only after checking that the lanes which matter actually have a conclusion - read the run's jobs, not the PR rollup, or look for the 'ci routing:' line in the run log ('gate'/'affected' ran lanes; 'metadata' ran none). To force a real run without changing a byte: an empty commit (git commit --allow-empty) produces a 'synchronize' event, and since the tree is identical it does not invalidate evidence captured at the previous SHA - state that, with the empty diff, rather than re-capturing.

verification.requirement: Before treating a PR's CI as evidence, confirm fast / format, fast / typecheck and fast / focused unit each have a conclusion (success/failure) and are not SKIPPED. When in doubt: gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/runs/RUN_ID/jobs --jq '.jobs[]|"\(.conclusion) \(.name)"' and check for 'ci routing: gate' in the log. Never cite an aggregate success as proof a lane passed.
